summary: The root لَبَدَ (labada) primarily means to stick or adhere, especially to the ground. It can describe a bird lying on its breast or a person staying fixed in a place.
lane: 1 لَبِدَ ذ , aor. لَبَدَ , inf. n. لَبَدٌ , It (a thing) stuck, clave, or adhered. (Msb.) -b2- لَبَدَ بِالأَرْضِ , aor, لَبُدَ , inf. n. لُبُودٌ ; (S, L;) and بِهَا ; (L;) and بِهَا ; (S;) It (a thing) stuck, clave, or adhered, to the ground. (S, L.) -b3- بِالأَرْضِ He (a bird) lay upon his breast, cleaving to the ground. (S, L, K.) -b4- (tropical:) He clave to the ground, concealing his person. (A.) -b5- Hence the proverb تَصَيَّدِى , [for تَتَصَيَّدِى , (tropical:) Cleave thou (addressed to a female) to the ground: thou wilt take, or catch, or snare, or entrap, game ]. (A.) -b6- Hence also, (tropical:) He remained fixed, or steady, and looked, or considered. (A.) -b7- لَبَدَ بِالمَكَانِ , (L, K, *) aor. لَبُدَ , inf. n. لُبُودٌ ; and لَبِدَ , aor. لَبَدَ , inf. n. لَبَدٌ ; (L, K;) and ; (S, L, K;;) (tropical:) He remained, continued, stayed, abode, or dwelt, in the place; (S, L, K; *) and clave to it. (L, K. *) -b8- لَبَدَ عَلَى عَصَاهُ , inf. n. لُبُودٌ , (assumed tropical:) He (a pastor) leaned upon his staff, remaining fixed to his place. (L.) -b9- لَبِدَ , aor. لَبَدَ , (S, L,) inf. n. لَبَدٌ , (S, L, K,) He (a camel) became choked by eating much of the plant called صِلِّيَان , suffering a contortion in the [ part of the chest called ] حَيْزُوم and in the [ part of the throat called ] غَلْصَمَة : (ISk, S, L, K: *) or had a complaint of the belly from eating of the قَتَاد [or tragacantha ]. (AHn, L.) -b10- See 4.
